== Biography ==
John was Christened in Glasgow, 19 Oct , 1771 in
Barony, Lanarkshire, Scotland to Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munro
<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M</ref>

An inherited adult account states that John was born about 1790; its identity with the separately cited 1771 child is unproved, and the claim is retained for comparison rather than adopted as this child’s birth.

Alexander Glasgow was born on March 17, 1799, in Colinton, Midlothian, Scotland. He was baptized on March 31, 1799, in the same place. His residence was in Greysmill. His father's name was John Glasgow, and his mother was Margaret Muckle. The baptismal records are part of the Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms collection, specifically from the year range 1738-1819. The archive reference for these records is OPR 677/2, and the entry is found on page 253.

This is compatible with the existing Kirknewton household associated with Glasgow-1304 and Muckle-67, but the transcripts do not identify either adult profile. === Colinton–Kirknewton working connection — 31 October 2026 ===

Alexander Glasgow-2695, the Midlothian agricultural labourer/ploughman, reports Colinton (also rendered Callington) as his birthplace, with census-implied births about 1801–1803. Alexander Glasgow-2718 was born 17 March 1799 and baptised 31 March at Colinton, residence Greysmill, explicitly to John Glasgow and Margaret Muckle. The distinctive birth parish, compatible two-to-four-year census age discrepancy and the family’s later Kirknewton context support identifying the childhood and adult accounts. John/Margaret’s recorded children at Kirknewton and East Calder in 1808–1814 provide a positive locality bridge to adult Alexander’s son John, born at Kirknewton about 1829. The first held son’s name John is only a minor, correlated clue. A bounded FamilySearch search for Alexander Glasgow, Colinton, 1795–1806 in Scotland Births and Baptisms returned the 1799child and two occurrences of the adult as a father; no closer childhood candidate was returned. This supports selecting the record-defined John Glasgow-1304 as the adult’s father at 65% subjective confidence, a new working attachment rather than a profile merger. <ref name="Colinton1799">[ https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4191802&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland Parish Births and Baptisms], Alexander Glasgow, birth17March1799/baptism31March1799, Greysmill, Colinton, John Glasgow and Margaret Muckle, OPR677/2 item3 p.253. Held provider transcript inspected22October2026; original register uninspected.</ref>

No inspected adult record explicitly names his parents; childhood-to-adult identity is inferred. The two-to-four-year age difference remains, and the bounded selected-localities birth index is incomplete: an unindexed Colinton child or a different adult identity for the 1799child could overturn the link. The census facts are held profile/index accounts, not newly read original images. The1799provider transcript was inspected earlier, original register uninspected. The Kirknewton Meikle entries are compatible family context, not independent proof of the adult identity. John-1304 represents the named Muckle father; his internally conflicting 1765/1771/c1790 childhood estimates and 78% upstream father assessment remain unresolved and unchanged. No mother attachment, exact birth replacement, wife identity resolution, or merger of 2695 and 2718 is proposed. The 1827blacksmith’s age 14/SouthLeith index details favour a separate person and do not establish the ploughman’s parentage.

The 1827trial comparison is superseded as a life-event attribution. The Crown Office precognition index AD14/27/25 and Edinburgh Lock-up House index HH21/8/1 p.11 both identify Alexander Glasgow, blacksmith, age 14 and born South Leith. The linked trial JC26/1827/326 names the same Alexander/John Paterson pair and housebreaking charge, with a 14-year transportation sentence. The age 14 and sentence 14 years are distinct indexed fields. The combined details strongly favour a younger circa 1812–1813-born accused, rather than the 1799Colinton child. Originals remain uninspected; this is a record-level identity correction, not a claim about the adult ploughman’s conduct. <ref name="Blacksmith1827">Scottish Indexes, [https://www.scottishindexes.com/adentry.aspx?adid=827025 AD14/27/25], [https://www.scottishindexes.com/jcdetail.aspx?jcid=1827326&pid=182732633 JC26/1827/326] and [https://www.scottishindexes.com/prisontranscript.aspx?prisonid=80101124 HH21/8/1 p.11], public index entries inspected30–31October2026. Original documents uninspected.</ref>

The proposed family amendment is to add [[Glasgow-1304|John Glasgow]] as the father of [[Glasgow-2695|Alexander Glasgow]], 65% probable. [[Glasgow-2718]] remains a separate possible childhood account. No live edit is claimed.
